_comment: Example config for the remote_diagnostic MCP server. Copy this to config.json (or point $REMOTE_DIAGNOSTIC_CONFIG at it) and edit for your cluster. JSON has no comment syntax, so keys prefixed with _ are documentation and are ignored by the server.
_comment_ssh: How to ssh in. domain is appended to bare hostnames (host -> host.<domain>); set it to "" to use hostnames verbatim. timeout is per-command seconds. user/key are the ssh login user and private key path; override at runtime with the REMOTE_DIAGNOSTIC_SSH_USER / REMOTE_DIAGNOSTIC_SSH_KEY env vars (those take precedence). Leave all of them "" to use the running account's own ssh identity — the right choice when the server runs under an admin account whose keys are already authorized on the nodes.
_comment_node_groups: Named groups the agent can target by role instead of guessing hostnames. Any group may be empty. The 'all' group is derived automatically as the union of every group below, so you don't list it here (set it explicitly only if you want a custom 'all').
_comment_control_host: Optional. Commands listed in cluster_wide_commands query a central controller and return the same answer from any node, so they always run once on default_control_host instead of fanning out over the targeted group. default_control_host must be one of the nodes above.
_comment_allowed_commands: The command whitelist IS the safety model: every allowed form must be read-only (commands may run with elevated privileges on the remote side). Map each base command to one of: null (any arguments); a list of allowed argument PREFIXES — the call's arguments must start with one of the entries, matched token-by-token ('osd df' allows `osd df detail` but not `osd out 3`), a token ending in '*' matches by prefix ('--query-gpu=*'), and an empty list allows only the bare command; or an object {"allowed": <null|list>, "denied": [tokens]} where denied tokens are rejected wherever they appear (use it to ban a read-only command's mutating flags). Anything not listed is rejected.
